newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: French far-right leader sides with Serb protests.
newsitem.headline: French far-right leader sides with Serb protests.

text.p: French far-right leader Jean- -Marie Le Pen on Tuesday sided with the Serbs protesting for the past two months against what he called the communist dictatorship of Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic.

"It appears to me that what is dividing this country is the communist dictatorship by President Milosevic," the president of the extreme-right and anti-immigrant National Front of France told a news conference here in Belgrade.
He said he came to voice support by French patriots for the Serbian people.
Le Pen arrived in the Serbian capital on Tuesday on a three-day visit at the invitation of the ultra-nationalist Serbian Radical Party (SRS) led by Vojislav Seselj.

Seselj was closely allied with Milosevic in the early 90-ties until they were brokenoff after Milosevic's acceptance of the Dayton peace accord which ended the 43-month war in Bosnia in November 1995.
Seselj has not sided with the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition which, together with Belgrade students, has been protesting against an election fraud for the past nine weeks.
International fact-finders have endorsed Zajedno allegations that it was robbed of victory in Serbia's 14 biggest cities, including Belgrade.
"We are fighting to topple Milosevic's leftist rule. But equally important for us is to prevent Zajedno from coming to power," Seselj said.
Seselj, who commanded a notorious paramilitary force in the six-month war against Croatia and later Bosnia, accuses Zajedno of treason.
"Since the World War Two no one had the audacity to carry a German flag in Belgrade. Are we going to import democracy from Germany?" Seselj asked.
He was referring to early days in the imaginative and peaceful demostrations when the protesters carried flags from various western nations, including Germany.
The Socialist-controlled state Television said the foreign flags were proof that Zajedno protests were run from abroad.
